items.title: Skitch Henderson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Milford, Connecticut, October 31, 1998
items.q: I made a record with Sinatra, the first record he made I played piano, “Night and Day” and “The Night We Called it a Day,” Axel Stordahl made the arrangements.

ctx.x: She sang in as we say the native language. So I spent the time looking at her diaphragm, feeling that if I watched her diaphragm I could understand what she was going about. And we did something like four sides in three hours with a big orchestra. It was unbelievable. She’s going to be with me in Tokyo this year. She did this as a preview. But there is no time. Time is gone. It’s gone. That’s a part of technology or part of greed. I don’t know what it is. I began in the record business when we got thirty-five…
Did you have to do that, isn’t there a six month period when you come to New York for the union, to get in the union?
